Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Greenville-Spartanburg SC
158 AM EST Sat Nov 28 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Rain amounts have increased across our western zones from Sunday 
through early Monday.

Rain chances have increased across our area towards the end of
next week.   

The aviation discussion was updated for the 06z TAFs.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1. Gusty winds will taper off across most of our area through
the morning with higher gusts lingering over the northern NC
mountains. Temperatures warm over the weekend.
2. A cold front is expected to bring rain and more gusty winds
to our area Sunday into early Monday, with dry/quiet weather in
its wake. Another weather system could bring more precipitation
by the end of next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Key message 1: Gusty winds will taper off across most of our area 
through the morning with higher gusts lingering over the northern
NC mountains. Temperatures warm over the weekend.

A broad/deep upper low will continue to lift NE and well away from 
our area today. In its wake, mid/upper level flow will become more
zonal with heights rising across the region. As the associated sfc
low moves further away from our region, profiles will continue to 
dry and mostly sunny skies will return today.  

We can expect low-end gusts of 15 to 25 mph to continue across the 
Upstate and Piedmont into the morning. Stronger gusts up to roughly 
35 mph are more likely to linger over the higher elevations of the
NC mtns and especially over the northern NC mtns. Another round of 
breezy winds is expected this afternoon across most of our non-mtn
zones, with gusts in the 15 to 20 mph range. The gusts should dissi-
pate this evening. High temperatures are expected to rebound back to
near-normal, if not slightly above, this afternoon. Values on Sunday
should be a few degrees warmer.


Key message 2: A cold front is expected to bring rain and more gusty 
winds to our area Sunday into early Monday, with dry/quiet weather 
in its wake. Another weather system could bring more precipitation 
by the end of next week.

A deepening upper shortwave over the Rockies is expected to induce
cyclogenesis over the southern Plains later today and into Sunday. 
The upper shortwave and associated sfc low continue to deepen as 
they move over the MS River Valley on Sunday, pushing a robust cold 
front across the Appalachians Sunday night. A stout pre-frontal 850mb 
jet of 50 to 60 kts is expected to precede the front, with a decent 
Gulf connection suggesting some potential for heavy rainfall late 
Sunday aftn and Sunday evening. The flood potential still appears
minimal given how fast the front will be moving. Most of the latest 
ensembles produce anywhere from 0.3 to 1.25 inches of storm total QPF 
over the western half of our CWA and less than 0.5 inches over our 
eastern zones. The 1+ inch area is mostly limited to the escarpment
where upslope flow is expected to enhance precip rates.   

Model fcst soundings continue to show weak lapse rates preceding this 
fropa and as a result, they produce very little sfc-based CAPE across 
our area. Shear profiles, however, remain impressive with good dynamic 
support from the upper shortwave. Thus, this system is expected to be 
a high-shear/low-CAPE type of severe threat. The main concern with this
system will likely be another round of gusty winds Sunday aftn through 
early Monday. Gusts may exceed 30 mph over our lower terrain, with 40 
to 50 mph gusts possible over our higher elevations as we mix into 
stronger winds associated with the jet. As such, a Wind Advisory may 
be needed for our higher elevations during this event. Following the 
front, dry/cool high pressure spreads back over the region and lingers 
thru the middle of the week with temperatures warming to well-above 
normal by the end of the week. 

Most of the long-range model guidance continues to develop another 
amplified upper shortwave/closed low to our west late next week. 
The associated sfc low and cold front are fcst to impact our area 
Friday into Saturday with precip chances increasing with this latest 
fcst. Temperatures are also trending warmer during this event, so 
it's looking more likely that only rain will occur over our area.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
At KCLT and elsewhere: VFR conditions will prevail at all TAF sites
through the forecast period. Low clouds have mostly dissipated
outside of the mountains, with only a band extending across KHKY,
which could allow for low VFR cigs over the next few hours. Low
clouds are mainly confined to the NC/TN border with only mid to
high clouds extending over KAVL. Otherwise, clouds are expected
to continue dissipating tonight, leading to clearer skies
during the daytime period outside of thin cirrus passing across
the area. West-southwesterly winds continue through much of the
forecast period, except KAVL as an upvalley wind persists with
lingering low-end gusts through tonight before subsiding by the
pre-dawn hours. Winds pick up again by this afternoon with low-end
gusts possible again, especially at the Upstate sites.

Outlook: A cold front will bring a brief shot of rain and associated
restrictions Sunday afternoon into Sunday night. Drier conditions
return early next week.
